newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Albright proposes NATO help for Albanian army.
newsitem.headline: Albright proposes NATO help for Albanian army.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday urged NATO to consider how it can help Albania restore and rebuild its armed forces.

"I believe NATO should now send a SHAPE assessment team to Albania in the very near future to determine how the alliance can help restore a functioning, democratically-controlled military to the country," she said in remarks to the new partnership council between NATO and non-alliance states.
Supreme Headquarter Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) is NATO's military headquarters in Mons, Belgium.

Albright gave no details. But she said the results of such a mission should be discussed in the new council -- officially called the Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council (EAPC) -- "so that we can all work together effectively to restore stability to that troubled nation."
Albania spiralled into crisis this year when financial pyramid schemes went bust, bankrupting thousands of Albanians and creating political turmoil.

A Italian-led 6,000 strong multi-national force was sent to Albania in early April to protect humanitarian aid convoys. France, Spain, Romania, Turkey, Greece, Austria and Denmark also contributed troops.

In a week in which NATO has made new strides in re- fashioning itself, Albright said Albania reflects "the kind of crisis we face in Europe and beyond in the years ahead and of the need for NATO and the EAPC, together with the OSCE (Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe) to focus our efforts on preventing conflict."
Aiming to adapt old institutions to new post-Cold War challenges, NATO is moving to take in new members and has negotiated special new security agreements with Russia and Ukraine.

It has also created an auxiliary group called Partnership for Peace for non-NATO members that "has made cooperation among our armed forces so smooth, continuous and successful that it now seems a matter of course," she noted.

"In other words, we have moved far beyond mere dialogue and cooperation. Today we are aiming at nothing than true integration of Europe and the transatlantic community. We are turning a Europe of shared ideals into a Europe of shared responsibilities," she said.

Albright said the EAPC must embody that goal as it gives Partnership for Peace a "political dimension" in which members can help shape joint missions as in Bosnia, harmonise defence planning and consult on arms control, terrorism, disaster relief and "the full range of peace support operations."
The new council "reflects our judgment that we must do more then just respond to crises, that if we wait for a threat to arise, we will invite a threat to arise," she said.
